model.name: Physical Item Instance
model.purpose: Represent any individual physical thing as a distinguishable instance so an agent can identify, classify, locate, hold, assess, trace, transform and retire it without minting a second master identity for type, configuration, stock, handling unit, assembly, asset or digital twin.
model.scope_statement: One real-world physical object that can be told apart from other objects, whether or not it is a trade item, an organizational asset, a cultural object, an industrial component, a natural specimen taken into tracking, or an unserialized thing later marked. The model carries only instance identity, instance-particular description, condition, lifecycle and disposition, location and containment membership, title and custody, and the event/provenance/evidence history that only an individual thing can have. Class, material, place, party, stock position, handling unit, as-built assembly and asset-value views are referenced, not restated.
in_scope: One real-world physical object that can be told apart from other objects, whether or not it is a trade item, an organizational asset, a cultural object, an industrial component, a natural specimen taken into tracking, or an unserialized thing later marked.
Condition, lifecycle and disposition of the individual thing.
Location and containment membership as links to place, handling-unit and assembly siblings.
Title and custody of the individual thing.
Event, provenance and evidence history that only an individual thing can have.
out_of_scope: Product types, GTINs, models and catalogues as class masters (sibling classifier, not this instance).
Product configurations and variants as class or option masters.
Stock positions, quantities on hand and inventory balances.
Handling units, logistic units and SSCC as packaging masters.
Premises, sites and places as location masters.
Material substances and material classes as constitution masters.
Asset registers, financial assets and ISO 55000 value-realization views as a second identity.
Digital twins, Asset Administration Shells and product passports as digital representations rather than the physical thing.
Living persons and living organisms as legal or biological subjects.
Lots, batches and class-level observations except as a classification or provenance input to an instance.
Software, rights, contracts and other non-physical entities except as referenced evidence or authority.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Product type / class master (GTIN, model, catalogue)
boundary_notes.distinction: Type-instance: a GTIN, model or product type classifies instances and must not be stored as if it identified one thing.
Variant-instance: a configuration classifies a configured instance.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Premises, handling units and as-built assemblies
boundary_notes.distinction: Containment: premises and handling units contain instances; assembly models compose instances; this model stores membership links, not those masters.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Asset register and ISO 55000 asset-value view
boundary_notes.distinction: Asset-view: organizational value, risk and AMS objectives project over the item and must not mint a competing identifier.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Digital representations (Identification Links, GS1 Digital Links, ESPR passports, AAS records)
boundary_notes.distinction: Representation-view: IEC 61406 links, GS1 Digital Links, ESPR passports and AAS records resolve to or describe the item.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Natural physical things versus human-made objects
boundary_notes.distinction: Natural versus human-made: CIDOC E22 covers purposely created objects; this model also admits natural physical things once tracked.
Identifier systems are alignments, not a requirement to use one scheme.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Property law and legal title registers
boundary_notes.distinction: Legal title is jurisdiction-specific and is recorded as a claim with basis, not as a universal property-law ontology.

bundles.name: Identity and marking
bundles.description: Tell this physical thing apart from every other thing by recording the identifiers it bears, who issued them, how they are marked, and which identifier is master.
bundles.rationale: Every later statement about the item is only as good as the binding between record and object: GS1 requires instance keys to be unique and non-reusable, IEC 61406 requires one Identification Link per physical object, and Object ID exists because marks can be copied, damaged or absent.

layers.name: Instance identifier set
layers.description: Hold every current and former instance identifier and the rule that one physical item has one master identity with optional aliases.

findings.name: Identifier priority and schemes
findings.description: An IndividualProduct is a single identifiable product instance distinguished by a serial number or other alphanumeric identifier. GS1 instance identification uses GTIN plus serial number (SGTIN), GIAI for an individual asset, or GRAI with serial when a returnable asset instance must be distinguished from its type. IEC 61406-1 requires a globally unique Identification Link string assigned to only one physical object. These schemes are alternative or coincident identifiers of one item, not competing masters.

questions.text: What is the authoritative master-system identifier of this item, in which register is it native, and what is its IRI if one exists?
answer_data: A date must not be supplied as the identifier.

questions.text: Which governed global identifiers currently denote this same instance (SGTIN, GIAI, serialised GRAI, IEC 61406 IL, ESPR unique product identifier at item grain, AAS globalAssetId), and which are aliases versus former identifiers?
answer_data: identifier_entries[] each with scheme, value, iri, role (master|alias|former|rejected), assigned_by, valid_from, valid_to.

questions.text: If no master-system or governed global identifier exists, what UUID or ULID did the adopting Dimension assign, and when was it assigned?
Does each recorded key actually identify this one object, or is it a type, lot, model or logistic-unit key that must be moved to a sibling classifier or handling-unit link?

data_elements.name: master_system_id
data_elements.description: Native identifier in the governing register.

data_elements.name: master_system_iri
data_elements.description: Resolvable IRI for the master identifier.

data_elements.name: dimension_uid
data_elements.description: Dimension-assigned identifier used only when no higher-priority identifier exists.

data_elements.name: identifier_entries
data_elements.description: Scheme, value, IRI, role, issuer and validity for each identifier.

data_elements.name: granularity
data_elements.description: instance, type, lot, logistic-unit or unknown.

artifacts.name: Instance identifier record
artifacts.description: One assignment or discovery of an identifier on an item, including scheme, value, IRI, issuer, role, validity and granularity judgement.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Item id plus identifier scheme and value, sequenced by assignment or discovery time in RFC 3339.

findings.name: Uniqueness, issuance and non-reuse
findings.description: A GIAI must be unique for each individual asset and remain unique well beyond the lifetime of the relevant records; if assigned to items supplied to customers it must never be re-used. The GIAI is allocated by the asset owner or manager and must not identify a trade item or logistic unit. An IEC 61406 IL string shall be a globally unique string assigned to only one physical object. Identifier reuse after disposal is a governed exception, not a silent recycle.

questions.text: Who issued each identifier (manufacturer, asset owner or manager, catalogue Dimension, regulator), under which prefix or namespace, and is that party still the issuing authority?
For each identifier, is reuse forbidden for a period beyond the lifetime of the item records, and has this value ever been previously bound to another item?
When title or custody changes, does this identifier remain with the physical object, get withdrawn, or get replaced by the new owner's identifier?
answer_data: GS1 states that whether a GIAI remains when changing hands depends on the business application.

data_elements.name: issuer_party_ref
data_elements.description: Party that allocated the identifier.

data_elements.name: reuse_policy
data_elements.description: Non-reuse constraint for this scheme and assignment.

data_elements.name: transfer_behaviour
data_elements.description: What happens to the identifier when the item changes hands.

data_elements.name: prior_binding_item_id
data_elements.description: Detected previous binding of the same identifier value.

artifacts.name: Identifier issuance and retirement record
artifacts.description: Issuance, transfer-behaviour and retirement or embargo of an identifier value, used to enforce non-reuse.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identifier scheme and value plus issuance or retirement event time; retirement never deletes the prior entry.

layers.name: Marking and data carriers
layers.description: Record how identity is physically borne on the object and whether that mark is still readable.

findings.name: Physical marks and carriers
findings.description: IEC 61406 attaches the Identification Link as a machine-readable 2D symbol or NFC tag on the physical object. GS1 keys are carried in GS1-128, DataMatrix, QR Code or EPC/RFID with explicit Application Identifiers (8004 GIAI, 8003 GRAI, 21 serial). Object ID treats inscriptions, markings and photographs as identification evidence, not as a single numbering scheme. A mark is a carrier of identity, not identity itself.

questions.text: What marking methods and data carriers are present on this item (engraving, stamp, label, GS1 2D symbol, RFID, NFC, IEC 61406 IL, handwritten accession mark), and where on the object is each applied?
answer_data: markings[] with method, carrier_type, placement, encoded_identifier_ref, applied_at, applied_by.

questions.text: Was each mark applied at manufacture, applied later, or discovered already on the object, and what are the event time and record time of that fact?
Does the carrier encode only a local serial, a GS1 Digital Link, an IEC 61406 IL URL, or another resolvable IRI, and what URL is actually encoded?

data_elements.name: markings
data_elements.description: Physical mark or carrier on the item.

data_elements.name: carrier_type
data_elements.description: 2D, NFC, RFID, engraving, stamp, label, accession mark, other.

data_elements.name: encoded_string
data_elements.description: Literal payload encoded in the carrier.

data_elements.name: placement
data_elements.description: Where on the object the mark is applied.

artifacts.name: Marking and carrier record
artifacts.description: One physical mark or data carrier on the item, with method, placement, encoded payload and application or discovery event.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Item id plus carrier type and placement, sequenced by application or discovery time.

findings.name: Legibility, cloning risk and distinguishing marks
findings.description: Object ID requires inscriptions and markings, distinguishing features and photographs because unique numbers can be copied, lost or never assigned. A cloned serial or unreadable tag does not by itself prove a second item, nor does it destroy the original item's identity. Condition of the mark is evidence about identification quality, not a new identifier.

questions.text: Is each identifier mark currently legible, damaged, over-labelled, removed or only photographically documented, and when was that assessed?
What Object ID-style distinguishing features, inscriptions or damage patterns uniquely describe this object even if serials are absent or cloned?
Is there evidence that a presented identifier is cloned, counterfeit, reused or bound to another item, and what is the confidence and evidence of that suspicion?

data_elements.name: legibility
data_elements.description: Current readability of a mark.

data_elements.name: inscriptions
data_elements.description: Object ID inscriptions and markings.

data_elements.name: distinguishing_features
data_elements.description: Non-serial features used for identification and recovery.

data_elements.name: suspicion_status
data_elements.description: Clone, counterfeit or reuse suspicion.

artifacts.name: Identification evidence pack
artifacts.description: Photographs, inscriptions, distinguishing-feature notes and legibility assessments used when numbers are missing, unreadable or disputed. Object ID requires photographs plus the nine description categories kept in a secure place.
artifacts.identity_strategy: One pack per item identified by the item id; each photograph and assessment inside keeps its own capture timestamp.

layers.name: Resolvable digital identity
layers.description: Align instance identity with URL/IRI carriers and digital representations without treating those representations as the item.

findings.name: Digital link, passport and shell
findings.description: IEC 61406-1 defines the IL string as a URL that is both the globally unique identification of a physical object and a pointer to related information. Schema.org requires that a GS1 Digital Link containing serial AI 21 appear only on IndividualProduct. ESPR establishes a digital product passport with a unique product identifier, unique operator identifier and unique facility identifier, accessed via a data carrier on the product. IDTA AAS gives the asset a recommended globalAssetId (IEC 61406 format) and optional specificAssetIds, while the Administration Shell has a separate mandatory id. These are representations and links, not a second physical item.

questions.text: What resolvable IRI or URL currently identifies this physical object (IEC 61406 IL, GS1 Digital Link with AI 21, DPP unique product identifier), and does it encode instance grain rather than type or lot?
answer_data: resolvable_iris[] with scheme, url, grain (instance|type|lot|unspecified), last_resolved_at, resolution_status.

questions.text: Which digital representations (DPP, AAS, other twin) describe this item, what are their own identifiers, and which of those identifiers are explicitly not the item master?
answer_data: representations[] with kind (dpp|aas|twin|other), representation_id, global_asset_id, specific_asset_ids, distinct_from_item_master (boolean).

questions.text: If a DPP or similar passport exists, what unique operator identifier and unique facility identifier are bound to this item instance, and at which production event?
answer_data: Treat operator and facility as referenced parties/places, not as item identity.

data_elements.name: resolvable_iris
data_elements.description: IL, Digital Link or other instance URL.

data_elements.name: dpp_unique_product_identifier
data_elements.description: ESPR unique product identifier when present; grain must be checked.

data_elements.name: aas_global_asset_id
data_elements.description: Recommended IRI for the asset in AAS AssetInformation.

data_elements.name: aas_shell_id
data_elements.description: Identifier of the Administration Shell, distinct from the asset/item.

data_elements.name: operator_identifier
data_elements.description: ESPR unique operator identifier of the economic operator.

data_elements.name: facility_identifier
data_elements.description: ESPR unique facility identifier of manufacture.

artifacts.name: Digital representation binding
artifacts.description: A link from the physical item to an IL, Digital Link, DPP or AAS record, recording that the representation id is not a second item master.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Item id plus representation kind and the representation's own identifier, which is never the item master.

bundles.name: Type-instance binding and instance description
bundles.description: Bind the instance to its class and configuration, and record only those physical particulars that belong to this one object.
bundles.rationale: GS1 states a GTIN does not uniquely identify each unit and Schema.org separates IndividualProduct from Product, so class facts are referenced rather than restated; what remains on the instance is the Object ID-style particular description that can only be true of this one object.

layers.name: Kind and configuration binding
layers.description: Resolve the instance to a product type and, where relevant, a configuration, without copying the class catalogue onto the instance.

findings.name: Type-instance boundary
findings.description: Schema.org IndividualProduct is a Product subclass for one identifiable instance; GTIN identifies trade item types and a Digital Link with serial AI 21 must not be attached to a generic Product. GS1 states a GTIN does not uniquely identify each unit; SGTIN (GTIN plus serial) does. IEC 61406-2 covers types/models, lots/batches and items, with the default assumption that an Identification Link identifies unique serialized objects unless otherwise indicated. The instance stores a kind reference, not a restated catalogue.

questions.text: What product type, model or other class does this item instantiate, in which sibling model does that class live, and with what resolution confidence?
answer_data: kind_identifier (GTIN, model number, GRAI type, other)

questions.text: If kind is unknown, disputed or the object is unique (museum exhibit, one-off), is the kind deliberately absent, a broad CIDOC type, or a local class, and who asserted it?
Has the resolved class changed over time (mislabel, retrofit, counterfeit revealed), and what is the history of kind assertions with event and record times?
answer_data: kind_assertion_history[] with kind_identifier, valid_from, valid_to, event_time, record_time, asserted_by, superseded_reason.

data_elements.name: kind_model_id
data_elements.description: Sibling class model, typically product type.

data_elements.name: kind_identifier
data_elements.description: GTIN, model number or other class key.

data_elements.name: resolution_confidence
data_elements.description: Confidence that this instance is of that class.

data_elements.name: kind_status
data_elements.description: resolved, unknown, unique-object or disputed.

artifacts.name: Kind reference record
artifacts.description: A dated assertion that this instance instantiates a class in a sibling model, with confidence and method.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Item id plus asserted class key and assertion time; superseded assertions stay in the series.

findings.name: Configuration and lot inputs
findings.description: A product configuration may classify a configured instance (variant-instance boundary). A lot or batch identifier is not an instance identifier; Schema.org places lot-bearing Digital Links on SomeProducts unless there is only a specific product. IEC 61406-2 separately treats lots/batches. Lot membership and configuration are classification or provenance facts on the instance.

questions.text: What product configuration or variant, if any, classifies this configured instance, and is that a sibling configuration master rather than an extra serial?
From which lot or batch was this instance produced or separated, and is that lot used only as provenance rather than as the item identifier?
answer_data: lot_is_not_instance_id (boolean, must be true for this model)

questions.text: Which instance-level master data attributes (EPCIS ILMD such as expiration) belong to this instance rather than to the type, and what is their validity window?
answer_data: ilmd_attributes[] with name, value, unit, valid_from, valid_to, source_event_id.

data_elements.name: configuration_id
data_elements.description: Reference to a configuration master.

data_elements.name: lot_id
data_elements.description: Provenance lot or batch, not an instance key.

data_elements.name: ilmd_attributes
data_elements.description: Instance/lot master data captured at commissioning or transformation.

artifacts.name: Instance master data snapshot
artifacts.description: ILMD or equivalent instance attributes (for example expiration) recorded at commissioning or transformation, distinct from type catalogue data.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Source event id (commissioning or transformation) plus item id.

layers.name: Instance-particular physical description
layers.description: Describe this object as found, without copying type-level geometry, material catalogues or place masters.

findings.name: Distinguishing description
findings.description: Object ID defines nine information categories for identifying a cultural object: type of object, materials and techniques, measurement, inscriptions and markings, distinguishing features, title, subject, date or period, and maker, plus photographs and a short description. CIDOC E22 Human-Made Object comprises persistent physical objects purposely created by human activity with objective physical boundaries; broader E18 Physical Thing includes natural items. Instance measurements and features override type defaults only when they are of this object.

questions.text: What measured dimensions, weight or other quantitative characteristics were taken from this instance, with unit, method, measurer, event time and record time?
answer_data: measurements[] with property, value, unit, method, measurer_ref, event_time, record_time.
Do not copy type-nominal dimensions unless measured or certified on this instance.

questions.text: If maker, production place, country of origin, country of assembly or production date are known for this instance, what are they, and which of those facts actually belong to the type?
Is this a human-made object (CIDOC E22), a natural physical thing taken into tracking, or unknown, and what evidence supports that classification?

data_elements.name: measurements
data_elements.description: Instance-specific quantitative characteristics.

data_elements.name: maker_ref
data_elements.description: Maker of this object when instance-specific.

data_elements.name: production_event_time
data_elements.description: When this object was produced or entered existence, RFC 3339.

data_elements.name: creation_kind
data_elements.description: Human-made versus natural versus modified natural.

data_elements.name: object_title
data_elements.description: Object ID title where applicable.

artifacts.name: Instance description record
artifacts.description: Object ID-aligned description of type label, measurements, inscriptions, distinguishing features, title, subject, date or period and maker, with photographs. Pure type facts should be referenced out.
artifacts.identity_strategy: One description per item identified by item id and revision time; photographs are referenced from the identification evidence pack.

findings.name: Material constitution as reference
findings.description: Object ID records materials and techniques; CIDOC uses P45 consists of to point from a physical thing to material. Constitution of an instance is a reference to material classes, not a local restatement of a substance catalogue. Instance-specific coatings, replacements or contamination are the only material facts that belong here.

questions.text: Which material-class identifiers constitute this item, in which sibling material model do they live, and is the statement typical-of-type or observed-on-instance?
Which instance-specific replacements, coatings, repairs or contaminants changed constitution after production, and when?
answer_data: constitution_changes[] with material_ref, change_kind (replaced|coated|repaired|contaminated|removed), event_time, record_time.

questions.text: Are making techniques recorded as instance evidence (especially for unique objects) or only as type process knowledge that should live elsewhere?

data_elements.name: material_refs
data_elements.description: References to material classes.

data_elements.name: constitution_changes
data_elements.description: Instance-level material changes after production.

data_elements.name: techniques
data_elements.description: Making techniques when they identify this object.

artifacts.name: Constitution reference set
artifacts.description: References from this instance to material classes plus any observed instance-level material changes. Not a substance catalogue.
artifacts.identity_strategy: One set per item identified by item id; each referenced material class keeps its own master identity.

bundles.name: Condition and lifecycle
bundles.description: Record what shape the item is in and where it stands in operational, existence and exceptional life, without turning ISO 55000 asset-value management into a second identity.
bundles.rationale: Condition, transient disposition, persistent business state and physical existence answer different questions and change at different rates; CBV separates disposition from persistentDisposition and ISO 55000 asset life is a value view, so all four are kept as dated statements rather than as mutable flags.

layers.name: Condition assessment
layers.description: Accumulate dated judgements of condition, damage, wear and repair of this instance.

findings.name: Condition history
findings.description: Schema.org IndividualProduct inherits item condition via OfferItemCondition. CBV 2.0 clarifies inspecting as a business step and adds dispositions such as conformant, completeness_verified and completeness_inferred. Object ID distinguishing features and photographs often encode damage that also serves identification. Condition is a time-stamped assessment, not a static attribute overwritten in place.

questions.text: What is the latest condition grade or OfferItemCondition-aligned value for this item, who assessed it, by what method, and at what event time versus record time?
What prior assessments exist, including after repair, inspection, damage or recovery, and do they form an ordered history rather than a single overwritten field?
answer_data: assessments[] each with the latest-assessment fields plus valid_until_superseded_by.

questions.text: Which defects remain open, which have been repaired or replaced, and which component instances were swapped (those swaps are also containment changes)?

data_elements.name: condition_grade
data_elements.description: Local or aligned condition grade of this assessment.

data_elements.name: offer_item_condition
data_elements.description: Schema.org OfferItemCondition alignment when applicable.

data_elements.name: defects
data_elements.description: Observed defects and their repair state.

data_elements.name: assessor_ref
data_elements.description: Who judged condition.

artifacts.name: Condition assessment record
artifacts.description: A dated judgement of condition, defects and method, with evidence. Assessments accumulate; they are not silently overwritten.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Item id plus assessment event time and assessor; assessments accumulate and are never overwritten.

layers.name: Lifecycle and disposition
layers.description: Separate transient operational state from persistent business state and from existence (created through disposed).

findings.name: Operational and persistent state
findings.description: EPCIS events carry a Why dimension including bizStep and disposition. CBV 2.0 introduces persistentDisposition as the non-transient business state of an object, adds business steps sampling and sensor_reporting, and clarifies commissioning, encoding, inspecting and removing. New dispositions include available, completeness_verified, completeness_inferred, conformant and container_open. Transient disposition and persistent disposition must not be collapsed into one flag.

questions.text: What is the current CBV-aligned disposition immediately after the latest event, and what is the current persistentDisposition if one has been set?
answer_data: Unknown if the item is not tracked in an EPCIS-like process.

questions.text: Which business step (for example commissioning, encoding, inspecting, receiving, shipping, packing, removing, sampling, sensor_reporting) produced the current state, and was the event ADD, DELETE or OBSERVE?
Is state expressed in CBV, a local asset-status list, a museum status list, or mixed, and where do those vocabularies conflict on this item?

data_elements.name: disposition
data_elements.description: Transient business state after the latest event.

data_elements.name: persistent_disposition
data_elements.description: Non-transient business state from CBV 2.0.

data_elements.name: biz_step
data_elements.description: Business step of the latest lifecycle event.

data_elements.name: action
data_elements.description: ADD, DELETE or OBSERVE.

artifacts.name: Disposition-bearing event
artifacts.description: An observation or process event that sets disposition and optionally persistentDisposition, with bizStep and action.
artifacts.identity_strategy: EPCIS event id or event hash that carried the disposition.

findings.name: Existence, commissioning and disposal
findings.description: ISO 55000 requires considering assets across the whole life cycle from acquisition through operation and maintenance to disposal or renewal, but an ISO asset is an item, thing or entity with potential or actual value to an organization and may be non-physical. Physical existence of an instance is therefore not the same as asset lifecycle. CBV commissioning and encoding mark entry into uniquely identified tracking. Disposal, destruction, recycling or consumption ends tracking of this identity; a transformation may generate successor identities instead of a mere status change.

questions.text: When was this individual thing produced, collected, commissioned or first seen, distinguishing physical existence time from first-tracking time and from record time?
Is the item still an existing physical object, transformed into successors, consumed, destroyed, recycled, or only administratively retired, and what evidence supports that?
After disposal, which identifiers are embargoed from reuse and until when, given GS1 non-reuse beyond record lifetime?

data_elements.name: existence_event_time
data_elements.description: When the object came into physical existence, RFC 3339.

data_elements.name: first_tracked_time
data_elements.description: When unique tracking began (commissioning or first capture).

data_elements.name: existence_status
data_elements.description: Whether the physical object still exists as this identity.

data_elements.name: disposal_mode
data_elements.description: Destroyed, recycled, consumed, exported from tracking, etc.

data_elements.name: successor_item_ids
data_elements.description: New instances generated by transformation.

artifacts.name: Commissioning or disposal record
artifacts.description: Evidence that the instance entered tracking or left the world of tracked things, including successor identities and identifier embargo.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Commissioning or disposal event id plus item id; embargoed identifier values are retained in the record.

layers.name: Exceptional states
layers.description: Cover loss, theft, seizure, recovery, deaccession and other rare states that ordinary in-use vocabularies omit.

findings.name: Loss, theft, seizure, recovery and deaccession
findings.description: Object ID exists because stolen and trafficked objects cannot be recovered without documentation, photographs and distinguishing features; INTERPOL and customs use that documentation. Unknown whereabouts is not the same as non-existence. Seizure, loan, exhibition and deaccession change custody or collection membership without necessarily destroying the object. These states lack a single global code list and must be recorded as explicit exceptional statuses with evidence.

questions.text: Is the item missing to its holder, reported stolen, seized by authority, in dispute, or merely not recently observed, and when was that status asserted?
If previously missing or stolen, when was it recovered or returned, by whom, and did identity, condition or custody need re-validation?
Has a museum, court or owner deaccessioned, forfeited or legally abandoned the item, and does that end title, custody, or only collection membership?

data_elements.name: exceptional_status
data_elements.description: Missing, stolen, seized, disputed, deaccessioned, or none.

data_elements.name: last_known_location_ref
data_elements.description: Last trusted location before loss.

data_elements.name: recovery_event_time
data_elements.description: When the item re-entered trusted tracking.

data_elements.name: legal_reference
data_elements.description: Police report, court order or customs file reference.

artifacts.name: Loss, theft, seizure or recovery case file
artifacts.description: Exceptional-status assertion with legal or operational evidence, last-known facts, and recovery or deaccession outcome. Object ID documentation is the cultural-goods form of this artifact.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Case or report reference of the reporting authority where one exists, otherwise item id plus assertion time.

bundles.name: Location and containment
bundles.description: Say where the item is, was, and what currently contains it, by reference to place, handling-unit and assembly siblings.
bundles.rationale: EPCIS separates read point from business location and CIDOC records former or current location, so whereabouts and parentage are kept as dated fixes and membership links that resolve to sibling masters rather than as a mutable pin on the item.

layers.name: Location observation
layers.description: Record current and historical whereabouts as dated fixes, not as a mutable pin with no history.

findings.name: Current and historical whereabouts
findings.description: EPCIS separates Where into read point and business location. CIDOC P53 records former or current location of a physical thing. A location fix is an observation with event time, record time, source and precision. Coordinates may supplement but do not replace a place reference. The newest trusted fix is current; older fixes remain history. Unknown location is an explicit state, not a blank.

questions.text: What is the current trusted location of this item as a place or premises reference, with read-point versus business-location if both exist, precision, source, event time and record time?
What ordered historical location fixes exist, including last-known location while missing, and which fix was superseded by which later fix?
answer_data: location_fixes[] with the current-location fields plus superseded_by
include fixes during transit and unknown-location assertions

questions.text: Is current location confidential (high-value, seized, private residence), and which disclosure scopes may see it?

data_elements.name: place_ref
data_elements.description: Reference to a place master, not a free-text address as identity of location.

data_elements.name: read_point_ref
data_elements.description: EPCIS read point.

data_elements.name: biz_location_ref
data_elements.description: EPCIS business location.

data_elements.name: location_source
data_elements.description: Scan, sighting, declaration, sensor or unknown.

data_elements.name: event_time
data_elements.description: When the item was at that place.

data_elements.name: record_time
data_elements.description: When the fix was recorded.

artifacts.name: Location fix
artifacts.description: A dated statement of where the item was observed or declared to be, with place references, precision and source.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Observing event id where one exists, otherwise item id plus event time and source; later fixes supersede rather than erase earlier ones.

layers.name: Containment and assembly membership
layers.description: Record parent containers and assemblies as links, without turning this item into a handling-unit or assembly master.

findings.name: Aggregation and handling units
findings.description: EPCIS AggregationEvent records packing and unpacking of child EPCs into a parent. CBV 2.0 adds container_open among dispositions. Handling units contain item instances; the handling-unit identity (for example SSCC) is a sibling master. GIAI must never identify a logistic unit. An item may be in at most one open logistics parent at a time unless an explicit multi-parent exception is evidenced.

questions.text: What handling unit, package, vehicle load or other logistics parent currently contains this item, with parent identifier, aggregation action history and event times?
answer_data: aggregation_events[] with action ADD|DELETE|OBSERVE, event_time, record_time

questions.text: If the item is not in a handling unit, is it loose at a place, installed in an assembly, or unknown, and which of those states is authoritative?
Was completeness of the parent verified or only inferred (CBV completeness_verified vs completeness_inferred), and does that affect trust in this membership?

data_elements.name: current_parent_handling_unit_id
data_elements.description: Sibling handling-unit instance that currently contains this item.

data_elements.name: aggregation_action
data_elements.description: ADD, DELETE or OBSERVE.

data_elements.name: completeness
data_elements.description: Verified or inferred completeness of the parent.

artifacts.name: Aggregation event
artifacts.description: EPCIS-style packing or unpacking of this item into or out of a parent handling unit.
artifacts.identity_strategy: EPCIS AggregationEvent id or event hash; parent handling-unit identity stays with the sibling master.

findings.name: Assembly membership
findings.description: An as-built assembly composes item instances. Membership is a component link with position or role and install/remove times. The assembly model is the composition master; the item remains itself. AssociationEvent in EPCIS 2.0 can record associations distinct from logistics aggregation. Installing a component is not a type change unless a transformation event says identity was consumed.

questions.text: Is this item currently a component of an as-built assembly, in which position or role, installed when, and what is the parent item or assembly identifier?
If this item is itself a parent, which child item instances are currently installed, and which have been removed or cannibalized?
answer_data: child_links[] with child_item_id, position_or_role, installed_from, installed_to, removal_reason.

questions.text: Did a composition change consume this identity and generate a new item (transformation), or is it the same item with different components?

data_elements.name: parent_assembly_or_item_id
data_elements.description: Parent in an as-built composition.

data_elements.name: position_or_role
data_elements.description: Slot, station or functional role.

data_elements.name: installed_event_time
data_elements.description: When the component was installed.

data_elements.name: identity_effect
data_elements.description: Whether composition preserved this identity.

artifacts.name: Component link
artifacts.description: Membership of an item in an assembly, with position or role and install/remove times. The assembly master is sibling WM-OBJ-012.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Parent item id, child item id and install event time; the assembly master holds the composition itself.

bundles.name: Title, custody and access
bundles.description: Distinguish who owns the item, who currently holds it, and who may see which facts, under owner stewardship.
bundles.rationale: CBV separates owning party from possessing party and CIDOC separates title transfer from keeping or moving, so holding, owning and record stewardship are three distinct series; disclosure sits with them because a serial lookup must not leak holder or location.

layers.name: Possession and custody
layers.description: Record holding periods and transfers of possession independently of legal title.

findings.name: Custody periods and transfers
findings.description: CBV 2.0 prefers PGLN to identify owning and possessing parties, explicitly separating ownership from possession. EPCIS TransactionEvent and ObjectEvent can record business transactions around custody. CIDOC models movement (P25) separately from title transfer (P24). At most one open custody period should exist unless a documented joint-possession exception applies.

questions.text: Who currently possesses or holds this item, under what basis (ownership, bailment, lease, consignment, loan, exhibition, repair, seizure, unknown), and when did that period start?
What ordered custody periods exist, including open and closed intervals, transfer events, and gaps when holder was unknown?
answer_data: custody_records[] with possessor, basis, start, end, transfer_event_id, gap_reason.

questions.text: What business transaction, receipt, sensor observation or attestation supports the latest custody transfer, and who attested it to whom?

data_elements.name: possessor_party_ref
data_elements.description: Current possessing party.

data_elements.name: custody_basis
data_elements.description: Why the holder holds the item.

data_elements.name: custody_start
data_elements.description: Start of this custody period.

data_elements.name: custody_end
data_elements.description: End of this custody period; null if open.

artifacts.name: Custody record
artifacts.description: A period during which a named party held the item, with basis, interval and supporting transfer event.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Item id plus possessing party and interval start; at most one open interval absent a documented exception.

layers.name: Ownership and stewardship
layers.description: Record title claims and the steward who governs the item record, without claiming a universal property-law model.

findings.name: Title versus possession
findings.description: CIDOC P24 transferred title of is distinct from keeping or moving an object. CBV owning_party is distinct from possessing_party. ISO 55000 defines an asset as an item, thing or entity that has potential or actual value to an organization, physical or non-physical; becoming an asset of an organization is a value relationship, not a new physical identity. Title is a claim with jurisdiction and basis.

questions.text: Who is asserted to hold legal title or equivalent ownership of this item, in which jurisdiction, on what basis, and is that distinct from the current possessor?
What title-transfer events exist, with from-party, to-party, instrument, event time and record time, including partial interests if evidenced?
answer_data: title_transfers[] with from, to, instrument_ref, interest (full|partial), event_time, record_time, jurisdiction.

questions.text: For which organizations is this item currently an ISO 55000 asset (has value to that organization), and is that recorded as a view over this item rather than as another master id?
answer_data: asset_view_refs[] with organization_ref, asset_register_id_in_view, view_model_id (WM-OBJ-022), not_a_second_master (boolean must be true).

data_elements.name: owner_party_ref
data_elements.description: Party asserted to own the item.

data_elements.name: jurisdiction
data_elements.description: Legal system of the title claim.

data_elements.name: title_basis
data_elements.description: How title was acquired.

data_elements.name: asset_view_refs
data_elements.description: Organizations for which this item is an asset, as projections.

artifacts.name: Title claim record
artifacts.description: A dated ownership claim with jurisdiction, basis and instrument, distinct from custody. Not a full legal-title register.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Item id plus claiming party, jurisdiction and claim event time; instruments are referenced, not restated.

findings.name: Owner stewardship of the record
findings.description: The registry assigns stewardship to the item owner. ISO 55001 requires an asset management system with policy, objectives and continual improvement for organizations that manage assets. Record stewardship may follow ownership, a delegated registrar, or a museum documentation authority. Stewardship of the record is an access-control fact, not a second item identifier.

questions.text: Which party currently stewards this item record, is that the owner, a delegated registrar or a documentation authority, and when did stewardship start?
Who may grant read or write access to which bundles of this item, and are grants time-bounded?
When title transfers, does record stewardship transfer automatically, remain with a registrar, or split (for example public passport vs private history)?

data_elements.name: steward_party_ref
data_elements.description: Party that governs the item record.

data_elements.name: steward_role
data_elements.description: Owner, delegated registrar or documentation authority.

data_elements.name: delegation_instrument_ref
data_elements.description: Basis for delegated stewardship.

artifacts.name: Stewardship record
artifacts.description: Who governs the item record and on what authority, including delegations and splits after title transfer.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Item id plus steward party and start time; delegation instruments are referenced by their own identifiers.

layers.name: Constrained disclosure
layers.description: Define public, counterpart and privileged views so location and holder are not leaked by a serial lookup.

findings.name: Passport versus full record
findings.description: ESPR digital product passports expose mandated product information via a data carrier while the EU registry stores identifiers rather than the full dataset. Schema.org IndividualProduct can be published as a public product instance. Object ID documentation is kept in a secure place and used for recovery. A serial lookup may answer existence and lifecycle status without exposing location or holder. These are projections, not separate items.

questions.text: For a caller who presents only a serial or IL, what fields may be returned (existence, kind, lifecycle status) and which must be withheld (location, holder, condition detail, owner)?
If a DPP or similar passport applies, which fields are mandated for public or regulator view, and which remain owner-only?
Which exceptional recipients (repairer, valuer, insurer, police, customs) have been granted which scopes, for which interval, and on what legal or owner basis?
answer_data: exceptions[] with recipient_ref, scopes, purpose, legal_or_owner_basis, valid_from, valid_to.

data_elements.name: public_fields
data_elements.description: Fields allowed in unconstrained serial lookup.

data_elements.name: withheld_fields
data_elements.description: Fields forbidden in public lookup, typically location and holder.

data_elements.name: disclosure_exceptions
data_elements.description: Granted exceptional access.

artifacts.name: Disclosure policy binding
artifacts.description: The item's current public, passport, counterpart and exceptional disclosure rules. Policy text may be shared; the binding is per item.
artifacts.identity_strategy: One current binding per item identified by item id plus policy version and effective interval; superseded bindings are retained.

bundles.name: Events, provenance and evidence
bundles.description: Record what happened to the item, who is responsible, how identity derived or changed, and what evidence supports those statements.
bundles.rationale: EPCIS supplies the operating history, PROV supplies responsibility and derivation, and Object ID supplies the evidence without which a recovered object cannot be matched, so every asserted fact stays traceable to an event, an agent and a piece of evidence.

layers.name: Process and observation events
layers.description: Capture EPCIS-style events as the operating history of the instance.

findings.name: Event dimensions
findings.description: EPCIS 2.0 records What, When, Where, Why and How. Event types are ObjectEvent, AggregationEvent, TransactionEvent, TransformationEvent and AssociationEvent. When includes event time and record time. Why includes bizStep, disposition and persistentDisposition. How includes sensor elements in 2.0. Instance EPCs must not be mixed up with class-level EPCs. Event hash identifiers and business-transaction hash URIs appear in CBV 2.0.

questions.text: What events in this item's history are known, with type, action, event time, record time, event id or hash, and which identifier of the item was observed?
answer_data: events[] with event_type, action, event_time, record_time, event_id, event_hash, observed_identifier, biz_step, disposition.

questions.text: Was each event about this specific instance, a class/lot of which this instance is a member, or mixed, and is class-level inference flagged as inferred?
What How-dimension sensor measurements accompanied the event, with quantity, unit, sensor id, and measurement time?
answer_data: sensor_elements[] with type, value, unit, sensor_id, measurement_time

data_elements.name: event_type
data_elements.description: ObjectEvent, AggregationEvent, TransactionEvent, TransformationEvent or AssociationEvent.

data_elements.name: event_time
data_elements.description: When the physical or business fact occurred.

data_elements.name: record_time
data_elements.description: When the event was recorded.

data_elements.name: event_hash
data_elements.description: CBV 2.0 EPCIS Event Hash ID.

data_elements.name: observation_grain
data_elements.description: Instance versus class-level observation.

artifacts.name: Item event
artifacts.description: One EPCIS-aligned event about this instance, including dimensions What, When, Where, Why and How.
artifacts.identity_strategy: EPCIS event id or CBV EPCIS Event Hash ID; where neither exists, item id plus event time and capturing system.

findings.name: Transformation and identity change
findings.description: EPCIS TransformationEvent records inputs consumed and outputs produced. PROV-O models activities that consume, process, transform, modify, relocate, use or generate entities, and relates entities with wasDerivedFrom. Cutting, melting, remanufacture, kitting and consumption may end this identity and mint successors; mere repair or component swap usually should not. The decision is an evidenced transformation, not an implicit status change.

questions.text: Did a transformation consume this item as input, and which output item identities were generated, with event time and record time?
From which prior items, lots or materials was this item derived, and is that derivation generation, assembly, split or other?
Is there a conflict between a recorded transformation (new identity) and a recorded repair (same identity), and which statement is authoritative?

data_elements.name: transformation_event_id
data_elements.description: Event that consumed or produced this identity.

data_elements.name: input_item_ids
data_elements.description: Consumed identities.

data_elements.name: output_item_ids
data_elements.description: Generated identities.

data_elements.name: derivation_type
data_elements.description: How this entity relates to its precursors.

artifacts.name: Transformation event
artifacts.description: An identity-changing process with inputs, outputs and derivation type. Successor items are new WM-OBJ-001 instances.
artifacts.identity_strategy: EPCIS TransformationEvent id; successor identities are new item records with their own master identity.

layers.name: Provenance responsibility and evidence quality
layers.description: Bind activities and agents to the item and grade the evidence that supports identity, location and custody.

findings.name: Generation and responsibility
findings.description: PROV-O defines an Entity as a physical, digital, conceptual or other thing with some fixed aspects; an Activity occurs over time and acts upon entities; an Agent bears responsibility. Core relations include wasGeneratedBy, used, wasAssociatedWith and wasDerivedFrom. CBV identifies owning and possessing parties as agents in the supply-chain sense. Provenance of the physical object is not the same as provenance of the database record; both may be stored, but they must be labelled.

questions.text: Which activity generated this item as a PROV entity, which agents were associated, and which entities were used as inputs?
Who is the responsible agent for the latest identity, location, custody and condition assertions, and are those agents persons, organizations or software?
answer_data: assertion_responsibilities[] with fact_kind, agent_ref, agent_type (person|organization|software), asserted_at.

questions.text: For each provenance statement, does it describe the physical object, the digital record about the object, or both, and how are those graphs separated?

data_elements.name: generated_by_activity
data_elements.description: PROV activity that generated the entity.

data_elements.name: associated_agents
data_elements.description: Agents responsible for the generating activity.

data_elements.name: provenance_plane
data_elements.description: Object versus record provenance.

artifacts.name: Provenance graph excerpt
artifacts.description: PROV-aligned generation, use, derivation and agent associations for this item. Inline only if a single generation fact exists with no further graph.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Item id as PROV entity; nodes reuse the activity, agent and entity identifiers of the source graph.

findings.name: Evidence and record quality
findings.description: Object ID requires photographs, a completed checklist, a short description and secure storage of documentation because recovery fails without evidence. CBV 2.0 adds certification list attributes and test/cert business transaction types. EPCIS 2.0 sensor elements are measurements that can corroborate events. Quality is a property of a statement (method, agent, evidence, confidence), not a single score on the item.

questions.text: What photographs, scans, certificates, sensor readings or documents support that this record denotes the physical object in hand, and where is that evidence kept?
answer_data: evidence[] with kind (photo|scan|certificate|sensor|document), hash, captured_at, capturer_ref, storage_ref, supports (identity|location|custody|condition).

questions.text: What confidence or completeness attaches to current identity, location, custody and condition, and is completeness verified or inferred?
answer_data: fact_quality[] with fact_kind, confidence, completeness (verified|inferred|unknown), method, last_reviewed_at.

questions.text: Which current statements fail identifier, time, granularity or uniqueness validation, and are they quarantined rather than treated as fact?
answer_data: validation_issues[] with rule_id, fact_ref, severity, quarantine (boolean), detected_at.

data_elements.name: evidence
data_elements.description: Evidence objects supporting one or more facts.

data_elements.name: confidence
data_elements.description: Confidence of a stated fact.

data_elements.name: completeness
data_elements.description: Verified versus inferred completeness.

data_elements.name: validation_issues
data_elements.description: Failed validation rules on current statements.

artifacts.name: Evidence object
artifacts.description: A photograph, scan, certificate, sensor payload or document that supports identity, location, custody or condition, with hash and capture metadata.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Content hash plus capture time and capturer; storage location is referenced, not embedded.

functions.name: Register physical item instance
functions.description: Create a new item record when a distinguishable physical thing is produced, collected, commissioned or first seen, assigning a Dimension UID only if no higher-priority identifier exists.
inputs: Entry mode: produced, collected, commissioned or first-seen
Candidate identifiers with scheme, issuer and granularity
Event time and record time in RFC 3339
outputs: New item record carrying exactly one master identity
preconditions: No existing item record already binds the presented instance-granular identifier
effects: Creates the item record and its first identifier binding
Assigns a Dimension UID only when no master-system or governed global identifier exists

functions.name: Bind or discover identifier
functions.description: Attach, discover or retire an instance identifier, recording issuer, marking, granularity and non-reuse constraints, and reject type, lot or logistic-unit keys as masters.
inputs: Marking or carrier details where the identifier is borne on the object
outputs: Identifier binding with role master, alias, former or rejected
preconditions: Item record exists
Granularity of the presented key has been judged

Records the non-reuse constraint of the scheme

functions.name: Resolve identifier
functions.description: Answer whether a presented serial, GIAI, IL, Digital Link or Dimension UID denotes a known instance, returning lifecycle status without location or holder unless authorized.
inputs: Presented serial, GIAI, Identification Link, Digital Link or Dimension UID
outputs: Existence answer with kind and coarse lifecycle status
Full item view when the caller is authorized
preconditions: Presented identifier parses to a known scheme or is treated as unknown
effects: Withholds location and current holder absent a grant
Logs the lookup for audit

functions.name: Bind kind and configuration
functions.description: Assert or revise the class and optional configuration of the instance as references to sibling masters, with confidence and history.
inputs: Class key and optional configuration id
outputs: Dated kind assertion, optionally with configuration reference
preconditions: Class and configuration masters live in sibling models and are referenced, not restated
effects: Adds a kind assertion and supersedes the prior one without erasing it
Leaves kind_status unknown or unique-object when no class resolves

functions.name: Record instance event
functions.description: Append an observation or process event with What, When, Where, Why and How, storing event time and record time separately.
inputs: What, Where, Why and How dimensions
outputs: Appended item event with disposition and optional persistentDisposition

Observation grain is instance-level or flagged as inferred from a class event

Never rewrites the event time of a stored event

outputs: Location fix appended to the whereabouts series
preconditions: Place identity is referenced from a place or premises master
effects: Supersedes the previous current fix without deleting it
Records unknown location as an explicit assertion rather than a blank

functions.name: Aggregate or disaggregate

inputs: Aggregation action ADD, DELETE or OBSERVE
outputs: Aggregation event and updated containment status

At most one open logistics parent unless a multi-parent exception is evidenced
effects: Packs or unpacks the item
Leaves the handling-unit identity with its sibling master

functions.description: Record assembly membership with position or role, distinguishing Association from logistics Aggregation and transformation that mints a new identity.
outputs: Component link with interval
preconditions: Association is distinguished from logistics aggregation
effects: Opens or closes a component link
Preserves item identity unless an evidenced transformation says otherwise

functions.name: Transfer custody
functions.description: Close the open possession period and open a new one with basis, parties and evidence, allowing at most one open custody record absent a documented exception.
inputs: New possessing party and custody basis
Transfer event or business transaction reference
outputs: Closed prior custody period and new open custody period
preconditions: At most one open custody period exists absent a documented exception
effects: Closes the open period and opens a new one
Does not change title

functions.name: Assert or transfer title
functions.description: Record a jurisdiction-specific ownership claim or title transfer, distinct from possession, and optionally bind an asset-view projection.
inputs: Owning party, jurisdiction and title basis
Instrument reference and interest full or partial
outputs: Title claim or transfer record
preconditions: Ownership is recorded as a jurisdiction-tagged claim, not as a universal property-law fact
effects: Adds a title claim distinct from possession
Binds any asset view without minting a second master identity

functions.name: Assess condition

Applicable legal regime or owner mandate

Does not copy the item into a new master record
Logs the disclosure

Representation identifiers including globalAssetId, specificAssetIds and shell id

inputs: Failing rule id and offending fact reference

Corrective statement with its own record time
