composition.purpose: Premises contains physical item instances. Whereabouts resolve to place or premises masters; the item stores location fixes, not a competing place identity.
Product type classifies item instances. GTIN and other class keys identify types; SGTIN and IndividualProduct identify instances. Class catalogues are not restated on the instance.
Product configuration classifies configured instances. Variant-instance boundary: configuration is a classifier, not a second serial of the same object.
As-built assembly composes item instances. Instance-level assembly membership is a component link; the assembly model is the composition master.

Asset lifecycle is a projection over an item. ISO 55000 assets are things of value to an organization and may be non-physical. An asset register must not mint a second master identity for the same physical thing.
Stock position references item type or instances. Inventory balances and positions are not the item. Serialized stock may point at instances; unserialized stock points at types.
Handling unit contains item instances. Nested packaging and SSCC logistic units are siblings. GIAI must never identify a logistic unit.

Instance constitution references material classes. CIDOC P45 and Object ID materials point at material, which must live in a substance/class sibling rather than being restated here. Sibling model id was not supplied in this registry extract.

Location fixes reference place identities. EPCIS readPoint and bizLocation and CIDOC P53 are place references. Place master id was not supplied in this registry extract; WM-BLT-002 covers premises containment.
IndividualProduct is the public web vocabulary for a serialized product instance. Alignment only. Schema.org IndividualProduct is product-centric and does not cover all physical things.

EPCIS/CBV supply event, disposition, party and aggregation vocabulary for tracked instances. Alignment only. EPCIS also describes class-level events and logistic units that are out of this model's mastership.

Identification Link is a globally unique URL identity and data pointer for a manufacturer-serialized object. Alignment only. IEC 61406-1 applies to units already given unique identity by the manufacturer; it does not itself define custody or condition.

composition.target: CIDOC CRM E22 Human-Made Object and E18 Physical Thing
composition.purpose: E22 Human-Made Object and E18 Physical Thing are cultural-heritage alignments for persistent physical items. Alignment only. E22 is human-made; this model also admits tracked natural objects. CIDOC title and location properties are used as alignments, not as claimed conformance.

The item is a PROV Entity whose generation, use, derivation and responsible agents can be recorded. Alignment only. PROV entities may be digital or imaginary; this model is restricted to physical instances.

composition.target: EU ESPR Regulation 2024/1781 digital product passport
composition.purpose: A digital product passport and its unique product identifier may be bound to an instance when delegated acts require item grain. Alignment only. ESPR identifier grain may be model, batch or item depending on product-group rules; do not assume instance grain.

composition.target: IDTA Asset Administration Shell Part 1 metamodel
composition.purpose: An AAS instance asset and globalAssetId represent the same physical thing digitally. Alignment only. AAS shell id and specificAssetIds are not item masters.

Equipment, vehicle, device hardware and cultural-artifact models specialize this instance core. Inbound specialization. Registry extract does not assign those model ids; specialized identifiers such as VIN, UDI and IMEI belong in those extensions, not as a second general item master.

owner_package_requirements: Name the steward party for each item record and the authority under which it stewards (owner, delegated registrar or documentation authority).
Declare which identifier schemes the Dimension issues or accepts, their issuing authority and their non-reuse horizons.
Declare the default disclosure projection (public serial lookup, mandated passport fields, counterpart grants) and the basis for exceptional access.
Declare the sibling models relied on for class, configuration, place, handling unit, assembly, stock and asset views, so that no sibling mints a second item master.
dimension.namespace_guidance: Item instances are reached under the navigation path NAV.PHY.OBJ.INST on the world-model record plane. Dimension-assigned UIDs live in the adopting Dimension's own namespace and are used only when no master-system or governed global identifier exists; governed identifiers keep the namespace or prefix of their issuing authority (GS1 Company Prefix, manufacturer IEC 61406 domain, regulator-assigned passport namespace) and are never re-minted locally.
registry_links: GS1 Company Prefix and key issuance by GS1 member organisations (SRC-003).
IEC 61406 Identification Link resolution published by the party controlling the link (SRC-008).
EU ESPR digital product passport registry, which stores identifiers rather than the full dataset (SRC-013).

canonicalization_rules: All time values use RFC 3339 with seconds and an explicit offset or Z, with event time stored separately from record or ingestion time.
Open intervals use a start instant and a null end; closed intervals require both.

Identifiers are stored in the canonical form of their governing scheme (GS1 Application Identifier or URI form, IEC 61406 Identification Link URL, ESPR unique product identifier) with the scheme named alongside the value.
JSON, YAML, Markdown, HTML, Git, MCP and MongoDB are projections of this model, not its semantics.
patch_rules: History is append-only: corrections are new statements with their own record time, not silent overwrites of event time, custody or condition.
No patch may change the event_time of a stored event.
Invalid or disputed identifier bindings are marked rejected or former, never erased.
Deletion of an item is administrative retirement plus identifier embargo, leaving a tombstone that preserves uniqueness.
compatibility_rules: Alignments to GS1, IEC, Schema.org, ISO 55000, CIDOC/Object ID, PROV, ESPR and AAS are semantic alignments rather than conformance claims and may be added without breaking the item master.
A newly encountered identifier scheme is added as an alias of the existing master identity, not as a competing master.
Sibling models (product type, configuration, stock, handling unit, assembly, asset view) may extend their own records as long as they reference this item id and mint no second master.

identity_priority: Authoritative master-system identifier native to the governing register.
Governed global identifier or IRI such as GS1 GIAI, SGTIN, serialised GRAI, IEC 61406 Identification Link, or an ESPR unique product identifier when that identifier is instance-granular.
UUID or ULID assigned by the adopting Dimension.
A date is not an identifier; multiple coincident identifiers are aliases or former identifiers of one item.
artifact_rules.timestamp_rule: All time values use RFC 3339 with seconds and an explicit offset or Z; where an observation standard distinguishes them, event time (when the physical fact occurred) is stored separately from record or ingestion time (when the statement entered the system).
artifact_rules.serial_naming_rule: Serial artifacts (identifier bindings, events, location fixes, condition assessments, custody records) are named by the item id plus the artifact kind and the RFC 3339 event time of the statement, and are ordered by event time; entries are never renumbered or reused, and corrections are appended as new entries.
artifact_rules.integrity_rule: A physical item instance has exactly one master identity. Product type, configuration, stock position, handling unit, as-built assembly, ISO 55000 asset view, digital product passport, Identification Link resolver and Asset Administration Shell may reference or project that identity but must not mint a competing master identifier for the same physical thing. Observations are appended; identifier values that leave tracking remain unique well beyond the lifetime of the records.

policies: Append-only event and assessment history; corrections are new statements, not silent overwrites of event time, custody or condition.
Identifier reuse is forbidden for customer-facing GIAI and for any scheme that requires uniqueness beyond record lifetime; retirement is an embargo, not deletion of history.
Owner or delegated steward governs the record; possessing parties may add observation events but cannot rewrite title.
Public serial lookup and mandated passport fields omit location, current holder and non-mandated condition detail unless an exception applies.
Location, custody and title are references to place and party masters; they are not free-text identity of this item.

read: Owner and delegated steward may read all bundles.
Granted counterpart scopes (repair, valuation, regulation, lawful recovery) may read named bundles, layers, findings or artifacts.
Unauthenticated serial lookup may read only existence, kind and coarse lifecycle status.
Mandated DPP or similar public fields may be read according to the applicable legal regime.
create: Manufacturer, first capturer or steward may create the item at commissioning, collection or first-seen.
New identifier bindings, events, assessments, location fixes and custody periods are creates of child records, not replacements of the item.
Dimension UID is created only when no higher-priority identifier exists.
update: Steward may update steward-held aliases, kind resolution confidence and disclosure bindings.
Current possessor may append observations; they may not update closed custody or title claims.
No update may change event_time of a stored event; record_time of a correction is a new event.
delete: Physical deletion of history is denied except where a documented legal erasure right applies to a specific artifact.
Delete of the item means administrative retirement plus identifier embargo, leaving a tombstone that preserves uniqueness.
Access grants may be revoked (deleted as authorizations) without deleting the underlying item.
Invalid identifier bindings may be marked rejected, not erased, to defend against reuse and cloning disputes.

roles.name: Item owner
responsibilities: Hold or assert title.
Steward the item record unless delegated.
Grant and revoke counterpart access.

roles.name: Current custodian
responsibilities: Hold the physical object.
Append location, condition and observation events.
Report loss, damage or recovery to the steward.

roles.name: Identifier issuing authority
responsibilities: Allocate GIAI, serial, IL or other governed identifiers.
Enforce uniqueness and non-reuse in the issuing namespace.
Publish resolution of Identification Links or Digital Links they control.

roles.name: Registrar or catalogue operator
responsibilities: Operate the Dimension register.
Assign Dimension UID when required.
Enforce integrity rules across siblings (type, stock, handling unit, asset view).

roles.name: Condition assessor
responsibilities: Perform inspecting business steps.
Record method, defects, evidence and times.
Not change identity or title.

roles.name: Auditor
responsibilities: Read append-only history.
Verify identifier non-reuse, custody continuity and provenance graphs.
Cannot mint identifiers.

roles.name: Recovery authority
responsibilities: Use Object ID-style documentation to match stolen or seized objects.
Receive exceptional location and holder disclosure on a legal basis.
Cannot become owner by mere possession of the record.

roles.name: Public lookup caller
responsibilities: Present an identifier.
Receive only the constrained serial-lookup or mandated passport projection.

access.default_rule: Deny all read and write except to the steward and to processes the steward has authorized; public existence lookup is an explicit narrow exception, not default-open.
exceptions: Lawful recovery, customs and court orders may obtain identity, distinguishing-feature and last-known location artifacts without owner consent where statute requires.
ESPR or other mandated passport fields are disclosed to the extent the applicable product-group rules require.
A time-bounded owner grant may allow a repairer, valuer, insurer or buyer to read identity, kind and condition without location history.
The current custodian may read operational location and condition needed to hold the object, without title instruments they do not already hold.
audit_requirements: Record actor, action, scope, item id, event time of the fact if any, and record time of the access or change, in RFC 3339.
Audit identifier bind, reject, retire and reuse-check outcomes.
Audit custody and title transfers, location disclosures, exceptional access, passport issuance and any delete or erasure.
Retain audit records at least as long as identifier non-reuse horizons for the schemes in use.

coverage.claim: This structure is a defensible wide-union instance backbone for distinguishable physical things, grounded in GS1 identification and EPCIS/CBV events, IEC 61406 Identification Links, Schema.org IndividualProduct, ISO 55000/55001 asset vocabulary as a view, CIDOC/ICOM cultural-object practice, W3C PROV, IDTA AAS representation and EU ESPR passport identifiers. It is not a claim of universal completeness, legal-title ontology, or conformance to any one of those standards.

checklist.notes: Master-system id, GS1 GIAI/SGTIN/serialised GRAI, IEC 61406 IL, Dimension UID fallback, alias/former identifiers, non-reuse and granularity checks.
Commissioning, CBV disposition and persistentDisposition, existence versus administrative retirement, disposal and transformation, exceptional loss/theft/recovery.
Kind and configuration classifiers, premises and handling-unit containment, assembly component links, asset and stock views, digital-representation bindings.
RFC 3339 event time versus record time on events, assessments, custody intervals, identifier validity and location fixes.
EPCIS event history, PROV generation/derivation/agents, lot as provenance not identity, object-versus-record provenance split.
Title claims distinct from possessing_party/custody; stewardship of the record; asset-value relationship as a view.
Granularity checks, uniqueness/non-reuse, cloned-serial suspicion, quarantine of failed statements, completeness verified versus inferred.
Default-deny, bundle/layer/finding/artifact scopes, serial-lookup and passport projections, lawful-recovery exceptions, audit of disclosures.
History is append-only; delete is retirement plus identifier embargo; legal erasure is scoped to artifacts; GS1 uniqueness beyond record lifetime.
Explicit ALIGN links to GS1, IEC, Schema.org, ISO 55000, CIDOC/Object ID, PROV, ESPR and AAS, with conflicts recorded rather than claimed as conformance.
Place-referenced fixes with read point and business location, unknown location, sensitivity of current whereabouts.
Accumulating assessments aligned to inspecting, OfferItemCondition and Object ID distinguishing damage.
GTIN versus SGTIN, IndividualProduct versus Product, IEC 61406-2 type/lot/item, lot as non-identifier.
CBV owning versus possessing parties; CIDOC P24 versus keeping/moving; open custody interval rule.
TransformationEvent and PROV wasDerivedFrom for consume/generate; repair versus new identity as an evidenced decision.
IL/DPP/AAS/shell ids bound as representations; WM-OBJ-022 asset view forbidden as a second master.

known_omissions: ISO 15459 unique identification of transport units and items was not fetched as full text and is a likely additional identifier-scheme alignment.
FDA UDI, ISO 3779 VIN, IMEI and other sector instance keys are omitted here and belong in specialized extension models.
National property, bailment, pledge, wreck and salvage law is not modelled beyond a jurisdiction-tagged title claim.
Basel Convention waste-shipment and other disposal-law processes are not sourced.
Living organisms and specimens as biological collecting events (Darwin Core) are not sourced; natural-object admission is only via CIDOC E18 alignment.
Fine-grained condition taxonomies (museum condition reports, ISO condition-monitoring series) were not fetched.
Full CBV and EPCIS enumerations are aligned by reference; only values evidenced in the retrieved standard summaries are named locally.
ISO 55000/55001 full text beyond the official overview, asset definition and lifecycle phrasing was paywalled; detailed AMS clause mapping is a gap.
EUR-Lex HTML fetch for ESPR returned empty in this run; DPP grain and registry behaviour rely on official CELEX identity plus retrieved recitals/definitions from search of the legal text.
Insurance, valuation, customs tariff of the instance, hazardous-goods instance state and calibration status are omitted.
conflicts: ISO 55000 asset (value to an organization, possibly non-physical) is not identical to a physical item instance; treating an asset register as the item master is a conflict with WM-OBJ-022 VIEW.

GS1 GIAI is assigned by the asset owner or manager and may or may not travel with the object; IEC 61406 IL is assigned by the manufacturer to a unit already given unique identity. Both may coexist; neither is universally master.
Schema.org serialNumber is unstructured text; GS1 and IEC 61406 are structured, namespaced identifiers. Alignment is semantic, not syntactic.
GRAI without serial identifies a returnable asset type; GRAI with serial identifies an instance. Using GRAI as if it were always instance-granular is a conflict.
ESPR unique product identifier may be specified at model, batch or item grain by delegated acts; binding it as an instance master without grain evidence is a conflict.
EPCIS permits class-level events; inferring instance location or custody from class events without completeness_verified is a conflict with instance mastership.
AAS globalAssetId, specificAssetId and shell id are three different identifiers; using the shell id as the physical item id is a conflict.
GIAI must not identify a trade item or logistic unit; using one physical mark as GTIN, SSCC and GIAI is a conflict.
CIDOC E22 excludes purely natural objects that this model's purpose (any individual physical thing) still admits under a broader E18 alignment.
regional_assumptions: GS1 key issuance depends on GS1 Company Prefix allocation by member organisations; not all jurisdictions or informal makers participate.
EU ESPR/DPP obligations and the 19 July 2026 registry duty are regional law with extra-territorial effects on goods placed on the EU market.
Object ID recovery practice is internationally promoted (ICOM, INTERPOL, WCO, EU customs) but is not a statutory identifier in every state.
Ownership versus possession is recorded in a way compatible with both PGLN supply-chain practice and CIDOC title transfer; specific common-law or civil-law estates are not assumed.
IEC 61406 and AAS practice is strongest in industrial equipment in Europe; consumer trade items more often use GS1.
Time zones and RFC 3339 offsets are required even where local operational systems store naive local time.
adversarial_checks: Cloned or reused serials: a matching identifier is not sufficient identity; Object ID distinguishing features, photographs and non-reuse checks must be able to split or dispute the binding.
Second-master attack via asset register, DPP, AAS or stock keeping unit: those records must hang off this item id, not replace it.
Lot-as-instance: a batch code or unserialised GTIN presented as an item master must be rejected or reclassified.
Handling-unit confusion: scanning an SSCC must not create or overwrite a physical-item identity.
Silent identifier recycle after disposal: GIAI non-reuse beyond record lifetime must block re-registration.
Transformation laundering: melting, splitting or kitting must either mint successor ids or be an evidenced same-identity repair, not an implicit overwrite.
Public lookup leak: serial resolution must not reveal holder or location by default.
Natural unmarked object: absence of a manufacturer serial must still allow a Dimension UID plus distinguishing-feature evidence, or the object cannot be tracked as an instance.
